newsitem.title: UK: UK welcomes Hyundai Scottish jobs boost.
newsitem.headline: UK welcomes Hyundai Scottish jobs boost.

text.p: The UK government on Tuesday welcomed the prospect of up to 2,000 new jobs being created in Scotland by South Korea's Hyundai Electronics Europe, part of the conglomerate Hyundai Group.

Michael Forsyth, secretary of state for Scotland, said the company's plans to establish two semiconductor plants in the Fife region of eastern Scotland involved two phases. The first means an investment of 1.0 billion stg and 1,000 new jobs.
The group also has plans "to invest up to 1.4 billion stg in a second phase, which will create a further 1,000 new jobs. Total employment...is expected to grow to 2,000," Lang added.

Ian Lang, the UK's trade and industry secretary, said he was delighted "that once again the UK has attracted a major investment project from Korea. We now have more than 20 Korean companies manufacturing in Britain and by far the largest share of Korean investment in the European Union".
Lang said the UK offered a favourable climate for business, had a skilled and flexible labour force and a first-class science and technology base.
Earlier Hyundai said the Dunfermline plant would begin commercial production of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips in December 1998 and was aimed at European markets.

H.K. Yoo, managing director of Hyundai Electronics Europe, said Hyundai aimed to be the world's second largest memory chip producer by 2000 and the plant "forms an integral part of our strategy to secure this leading position in world markets".

"The decision to build our new facility in Scotland was made all the easier when we considered the advantages whch a Scottish base could offer -- skilled labour, a cost competitive operating environment, a well-developed electronics infrastructure and close proximity of some of our major customers," he added.
The Scottish Office said the project would also create significant indirect and induced jobs.

The office said in a statement that the construction of new buildings alone "is expected to generate over 1,600 construction jobs". The plant will consist of two facilities on one site, built in two phases.
